summary.text: The tensor product V⊗W of two vector spaces V and W over the same field is itself a vector space, with a bilinear map sending each pair (v, w) to an element v⊗w.
Every element of V⊗W is a sum of elementary tensors, which are elements of the form v⊗w.
Given bases for the two spaces, a basis of the tensor product is formed by all products of one basis element from each.

facts.label: Elementary tensors
facts.value: Every element is a sum of them

facts.label: Basis
facts.value: All products of a basis element of V with one of W

facts.label: Dimension
facts.value: For finite dimensions, the product of the two dimensions

facts.label: Universal property
facts.value: Every bilinear map factors uniquely through a linear map

facts.label: In physics
facts.value: General relativity describes gravity with the metric tensor field

items.prompt: Two finite-dimensional vector spaces have dimensions 3 and 4. What is the dimension of their tensor product?
items.explain: When both spaces are finite-dimensional, the dimension of the tensor product is the product of their dimensions.

items.prompt: One space has a basis of 2 elements and the other a basis of 3 elements. How are basis elements of the tensor product obtained?

options.label: By pairing each basis element of one with each of the other
By adding one basis element from each space
By keeping only the matching basis positions
By listing both bases one after the other

items.explain: A basis of the tensor product is formed by all tensor products of a basis element of one space with a basis element of the other.

items.prompt: You pick an arbitrary element of a tensor product. What form can you count on it having?

options.label: A single product of two vectors
A sum of products of two vectors
A single vector from one of the spaces
A basis element of one of the spaces

items.explain: The elementary tensors span the tensor product, so every element is a sum of elementary tensors, though not necessarily a single one.

items.prompt: You have a bilinear map from pairs of vectors into some other space Z. What does the tensor product do for such a map?

options.label: It turns the map into a basis of Z
It makes the map equal to zero
It replaces the map with several unrelated maps
It matches the map with one unique linear map to Z

items.explain: A bilinear map from the pairs into Z factors uniquely through a linear map from the tensor product to Z, so it captures all bilinear maps.

items.prompt: You arrange the coordinates of two vectors into a rectangular array. Which familiar operation does the tensor product abstract beyond coordinates?

options.label: The sum of the two vectors
The outer product
The length of each vector
The inverse of each vector

items.explain: The coordinate array of x⊗y is the outer product of the coordinate vectors of x and y, so the tensor product generalizes the outer product.

items.prompt: In general relativity, how is the gravitational field described?

options.label: By a single number for all of space-time
By one vector shared by the whole space
By a metric tensor field, with one tensor at each point
By a basis chosen once and never changed

items.explain: The metric tensor is a tensor field with one tensor at each point of the space-time manifold.
